recent_commits.message: The OpenScales OSD export now exists end-to-end. Work spanned three files:
recent_commits.body:
R/data_check_helpers.R — two shared, package-level helpers (so both the module and the converter can call them):

.osd_safe_code() — spec-valid code sanitizer.
.osd_code_and_provenance() — the three-tier provenance/code minting (dictionary → bare official code or curated METACHECK-; manuscript → METACHECK-; self-generated → METACHECK-GEN-), each with a human-readable provenance sentence.
inst/modules/codebook_check.R — rewrote .scales_to_osd(scale_groups, columns_df, labels_df, dict):

Spec-conformant structure: osd_version, definition.{scale_info, likert_options, items}, translations.en, plus a namespaced definition.metacheck block for provenance/confidence/source (kept out of the spec objects).
likert_options lets the codebook lead — decodes value_labels for range + anchor labels (source:"codebook"); falls back to observed min/max/n_unique from data_check stats (source:"observed"); omitted entirely when nothing is scale-shaped (no invention).
translations.en carries codebook item wording; text_key points at it per spec.
Named groups flagged write=TRUE; unnamed detections write=FALSE (report-only, no file).
R/psychds-convert.R — the file writer + cross-reference:

.osd_write_scales() writes one scales/{CODE}/{CODE}.osd per named scale (pretty JSON) under the dataset root.
.osd_write_readme_section() appends a "Psychometric scales" section to the root README.md explaining the three provenance markers and listing every scale (your "general README" decision).
Added metacheck:scale code + source to variableMeasured, so Psych-DS variables cross-reference their OSD definition.
n_scales added to the return list and completion message.

recent_commits.body:
`scripts/verify_corpus.py` now gets everything from article-finder: the expected
paper set, every PDF, and every baseline. No directory glob, no
`../PDFextractor/test-pdfs` coupling, no `DOCPLUCK_SPIKE_BASELINE_DIR`, no
`docs/superpowers/` default path. Papers are addressed by canonical key
(`--paper 10.1177/19485506211056761`).

**The coverage defect.** The gate derived its corpus from `glob("*.md")` and
printed `N / N` where N was whatever it found -- so a half-present corpus
reported a clean pass and a vanished one reported nothing at all. A denominator
computed from the numerator can only ever say 100%. It now comes from
`papers-with-view`, and three states are kept distinct:

  nothing resolvable        SKIP,    exit 0   (this machine has no corpus)
  some but not all          PARTIAL, exit 1   (the silent-shrink bug)
  all resolved              PASS/WARN/FAIL

New `PDF_DRIFT` status: the repository's copy of a paper is not the
manifestation the baseline was built from. Rendering one and comparing it to a
baseline built from the other measures nothing, and would print the difference
as a docpluck regression -- publisher PDF, arXiv preprint and PMC author
manuscript share a DOI but not bytes. It surfaced three such papers immediately.

**Re-baselined onto the repository's own copies**, which removes PDF_DRIFT by
construction: the artifact and the input the gate re-renders are now the same
bytes. Done only after all 26 papers verified against the 2026-05-10 prototype
baseline with ZERO failures (23 in the corpus run, 3 individually once their
drift was diagnosed) -- a baseline captured from unverified output bakes in
whatever was wrong at capture time. The prototype set stays registered as
`render-baseline__docpluck-splice-spike@2026.05.10` and is still selectable via
`--baseline-view`.

Result: 26 / 26 PASS, COVERAGE 26 / 26, exit 0.

Three lookup bugs found and fixed on the way, each of which had made a real
paper report as simply absent:

- `10.1093/sf/soaf022` keys as `10.1093__sf__soaf022`; replacing only the FIRST
  `__` produced a DOI matching nothing. Every `__` is an encoded `/`.
- Two PDFs were ingested under a non-normalized mixed-case DOI, so the
  lower-cased gold key could never find them. Fixed in `ingest-local-pdf.py`
  (it now uses `_lib.normalize_doi` rather than a hand-rolled prefix strip), and
  5 pre-existing unreachable index keys were normalized or removed.
- `verified == 0` returned exit 0 as a clean SKIP even when every paper had
  ERRORed or drifted -- a green run reported because everything failed. It now
  skips only when nothing was ever attempted.

Also: LESSONS L-013, a CLAUDE.md hard rule, and the qa/review/iterate skills
updated to read the COVERAGE line rather than the PASS count, and to treat
PDF_DRIFT as "nothing was compared" rather than as a render defect.

recent_commits.message: fix(normalize): refuse a sign flip against a CI that cannot hold a negative (v2.4.123)
recent_commits.body:
docpluck rendered an IMPOSSIBLE F-statistic. maier Table 9's row is

    Target article | 1, 114 | 2.00 | .16 | N/A | .02 | [.00, .09]

-- an F, its p, its partial eta-squared, and the CI OF THE ETA-SQUARED. W0d
(recover_minus_via_ci_pairing) repairs a font corruption where a minus is read
as '2', accepting the flip when the corrected value lands inside a paired CI and
the literal does not. It paired the F-statistic with the eta-squared's CI: -.00
is inside [.00, .09] and 2.00 is not, so it fired, and the render carried

    F = -.00

An F-statistic is a ratio of sums of squares -- non-negative by construction --
so the output was not merely wrong but arithmetically impossible. Both text
channels confirm the source reads 2.00; the library manufactured the sign.

Fix: refuse the pairing when the CI's LOWER bound is >= 0. A wholly non-negative
interval cannot contain a negative, so containment is satisfiable only
degenerately (-.00 clipping the zero edge), which is evidence of MIS-PAIRING
rather than corruption. Keying on the interval's arithmetic instead of on F
specifically covers every non-negative statistic that can sit beside a
non-negative CI (F, chi-square, R2, eta2, odds ratios, variance components)
without enumerating them, and cannot disarm a genuine recovery -- a truly
negative estimate always has a CI admitting negatives.

Evidence:
- tests written against the unfixed code and watched FAIL, then pass;
- all 31 pre-existing W0d tests stay green, incl. the efendic B-column
  recoveries the rule exists for;
- corpus guard-diff, all 152 PDFs rendered twice (guard on vs off):
  2 false positives removed (the maier article and its a downstream consumer duplicate),
  0 regressions, every other paper byte-identical;
- suite 1962 passed, 3 xfail (the P1 table defects stay armed).

Companion to the REJECTED W0b-col recovery: that failed because column consensus
is not per-record evidence. This is the converse -- per-record containment IS the
right evidence, but only when the record paired is the right one. A containment
test silently assumes the CI belongs to the token it pairs with; verify that is
arithmetically possible first.

for a source that reads "from 3 to 15" -- the library DELETED a published scale
bound and wrote an operator in its place. Both text channels confirm the source
says 3; the raw-text channel rendered the same sentence correctly a hundred
lines earlier, so one document carried the same fact right and wrong at once.

Not paper-specific: any "from 3 to N" / "between 3 and N" reaching a table cell
was affected, in any publisher's paper.

Root cause: W0i's only pre-digit guard was _TIMES_REFERENCE_WORD_RE, a list of
reference NOUNS (Model|Study|Table|Figure|...) that makes "Model 3 predictor" a
genuine ordinal. "from" is not a reference noun, so the guard had nothing to
say, while "from 3 to" matches W0i's letter-space-3-space-letter signature
exactly. A vocabulary list cannot defend a grammatical position -- it is always
missing the next word.

Fix: guard on the grammatical FRAME instead. A range is from|between BEFORE the
digit AND to|and|through|until AFTER it, with BOTH halves required -- a lone
trailing "to" could be a wrapped predictor ("Attitude 3 to risk"), and a lone
leading "from" is likewise ambiguous. A frame generalises across publishers.

Evidence:
- new tests written against the unfixed code and watched FAIL, then pass;
- full-corpus pdftotext sweep (all 152 PDFs): 8 range-frame-with-3 sites across
  5 distinct articles, out of 380 range frames overall -- all 5 pinned as
  regression cases. The sweep is why the guard covers "between ... and": maier's
  Bayes factors and bmc_med_3's lesion diameters use it, and a from-only guard
  would have left them exposed;
- targeted production-path guard-diff (each paper rendered twice, guard on vs

unchanged: the normalize fix is complexity-only, matching is byte-identical.

Two false-negative classes in the guard that decides whether a whitespace/char
grid is a real DATA table:

(a) _CAPTION_LABEL_RE was UNANCHORED, so a mid-sentence CROSS-REFERENCE in a
    footnote/prose cell ("...al. (2007) in Table 8.", "...in Figure 2. We
    summarized...") read as an absorbed caption and condemned the whole grid.
    An absorbed caption always BEGINS its cell; a reference has sentence text
    before it. Anchored to ^\s*, matching the discipline
    camelot_extract._CAPTION_ROW_PATTERN already documents (its comment notes
    anchoring is why an inline "see Table 2" does not match).

(b) the clean-data-cell test matched a SINGLE numeric token, so every
    multi-token APA COMPOSITE scored as non-data: 2.84 [1.89] (mean [SD]),
    3.47 [1.23] (170) (mean [SD] (n)), 2.84 +/- 1.89, 0.42***. A descriptives
    table built from them scored clean_data_rows=0 and was discarded as prose.
    Replaced the shape regex with a NUMERIC-DOMINANCE test (_cell_is_clean_data:
    digit-bearing AND free of substantive words), which generalises instead of
    chasing each composite with another alternation. The prose side is unmoved,
    so absorbed body text is still rejected.

101-PDF guard-diff: 24 tables recover (up from 20 at v2.4.120), 0 regressed,
0 foreign-caption acceptances.

A SECOND quadratic regex, and why the first fix looked complete but wasn't:
v2.4.120 bounded _CI_UPPER_DROPPED_RE and reported the ReDoS resolved. It was
not — normalize_text still scaled ~4-5x per doubling. It was missed because the
check was an absolute WALL-CLOCK budget, which passed alone and failed only
under parallel load, so it read as flakiness. Rewritten as a SCALING RATIO
(load-independent: contention inflates both measurements together) it failed
consistently, turning noise into signal.

Instrumenting every COMPILED pattern's .sub() via re.compile interception (a
module-level sweep misses these — they live inside a list literal, and reported
0.000s) attributed 3.165s of 3.7s at n=20000 to the Royal Society running-footer
pattern in _WATERMARK_PATTERNS, whose leading unbounded \d+ starts a match
attempt at every digit and then fails. Bounding it to \d{1,6} (a page number is
never longer) is ~1370x faster on the pattern (4.53s -> 0.0033s) and ~50x
end-to-end (normalize_text 4.85s -> 0.044s at n=20000), now genuinely linear at
~2.0x per doubling, with both real footer forms matched identically. A
lookahead-anchored variant was tried first and MEASURED WORSE (6.4s vs 3.2s) —
discarded rather than reasoned about.

This permanently removes the flakiness from
test_regex_no_catastrophic_backtracking, which prior handoffs recorded as a
load-sensitive perf test. It was a real, long-standing performance defect all
along. Full suite also runs ~10 min faster (24:51 vs 37:19).

recent_commits.body:
_cluster_into_rows measures the y-gap to the PREVIOUS WORD, not the row's anchor.
Words sort by (top, x0), so in a table with wrapped or vertically staggered cells
the running 'previous top' creeps forward in sub-threshold steps and the threshold
is never crossed — an unbounded chain merge. chan_feldman Table 3 holds 266 words
at 47 distinct y-positions with 0.3-7.4pt gaps against an 11.4pt threshold, and
clusters into 3 rows spanning 240pt: a 10-row table smeared into 3, which then
fails the grid guards on its own 'merits' and falls to the truncating raw_text
fallback.

The anchor-relative fix was implemented and REVERTED. In isolation it looked
excellent (chan T3 3->22 rows; T2 0->108 cells; T9 0->14 cells; maier T8/T11
gained cells) but it broke 9 real-PDF tests across 4 files, because a real row
can legitimately be TALL: xiao Table 4's row 2 spans 94.4pt as a multi-line
stacked data block, and a hard anchor cap shatters it. The previous-word test
under-splits; a naive anchor cap over-splits. Neither rule alone is correct.

Ships the reproduction as xfail(strict) so the defect stays visible and a correct
fix XPASSes loudly, plus three plain-assert companions pinning behaviour that must
not regress while it is solved. FINDINGS doc records the measurements and three
candidate directions (re-merge on shared column occupancy; explicit chain-merge
signature detection; derive the row grid from the most stable column).

recent_commits.message: fix(tables): a table's own caption no longer condemns its own table (v2.4.120)
recent_commits.body:
RC-T cycle 4. _whitespace_grid_is_clean rejects any grid containing a
"Table N."/"Figure N." cell — the signature of a region that absorbed a
NEIGHBOURING table's caption. But _region_for_caption builds every region as
_union(caption_bbox, geom_bbox), so a caption-anchored region ALWAYS contains
its own caption by construction. The guard therefore condemned EVERY region
grid: whitespace_cells returned 0 cells corpus-wide (19/19 chan_feldman+maier
regions) and each table fell to the raw_text fallback, which truncates rows.
The guard's own comment said the marker proves the region absorbed "an adjacent
table's (or its own) caption" — the "or its own" clause was the bug.

The exemption is IDENTITY-based, not position-based: the anchoring caption's
number is threaded from the region spec / region.caption_match into the guard,
and a caption cell is exempt only when it names THAT exact number, sits in a
leading row, and is the first such match — per-CELL, and opt-in so the
auto-detect path keeps the strict legacy behaviour.

A position-only draft was written and REJECTED in cross-model review (codex);
all three of its holes reproduced locally: a neighbour's caption in a leading
row blessed as "own" (publishing another table's data), (r,c) sort order picking
the leftmost caption on side-by-side pages, and a whole-ROW exemption letting a
second Table/Figure caption ride along. Each is pinned by a regression test.

repos.readme_excerpt:
Free, open-source AI academic paper reviewer that outperforms popular paid AI reviewers.

You provide your own API key and pay the LLM provider directly — typically **under $2 per review**.

Don't want to run it locally? Use the [web interface](https://coarse.ink/) instead.


Get an API key from [OpenRouter](https://openrouter.ai/keys) (free to sign up), then:

```bash
uvx coarse-ink review paper.pdf --api-key sk-or-v1-YOUR_KEY
```

That's it. The review is written to `paper_review.md` in the current directory.


coarse requires Python 3.12+. If you don't have `uvx`, install [uv](https://docs.

highlights.message: fix(qa): the corpus gate asks the custodian what it should cover, not the disk
highlights.body:
`scripts/verify_corpus.py` now gets everything from article-finder: the expected
paper set, every PDF, and every baseline. No directory glob, no
`../PDFextractor/test-pdfs` coupling, no `DOCPLUCK_SPIKE_BASELINE_DIR`, no
`docs/superpowers/` default path. Papers are addressed by canonical key
(`--paper 10.1177/19485506211056761`).

**The coverage defect.** The gate derived its corpus from `glob("*.md")` and
printed `N / N` where N was whatever it found -- so a half-present corpus
reported a clean pass and a vanished one reported nothing at all. A denominator
computed from the numerator can only ever say 100%. It now comes from
`papers-with-view`, and three states are kept distinct:

  nothing resolvable        SKIP,    exit 0   (this machine has no corpus)
  some but not all          PARTIAL, exit 1   (the silent-shrink bug)
  all resolved              PASS/WARN/FAIL

New `PDF_DRIFT` status: the repository's copy of a paper is not the
manifestation the baseline was built from. Rendering one and comparing it to a
baseline built from the other measures nothing, and would print the difference
as a docpluck regression -- publisher PDF, arXiv preprint and PMC author
manuscript share a DOI but not bytes. It surfaced three such papers immediately.

**Re-baselined onto the repository's own copies**, which removes PDF_DRIFT by
construction: the artifact and the input the gate re-renders are now the same
bytes. Done only after all 26 papers verified against the 2026-05-10 prototype
baseline with ZERO failures (23 in the corpus run, 3 individually once their
drift was diagnosed) -- a baseline captured from unverified output bakes in
whatever was wrong at capture time. The prototype set stays registered as
`render-baseline__docpluck-splice-spike@2026.05.10` and is still selectable via
`--baseline-view`.

Result: 26 / 26 PASS, COVERAGE 26 / 26, exit 0.

Three lookup bugs found and fixed on the way, each of which had made a real
paper report as simply absent:

- `10.1093/sf/soaf022` keys as `10.1093__sf__soaf022`; replacing only the FIRST
  `__` produced a DOI matching nothing. Every `__` is an encoded `/`.
- Two PDFs were ingested under a non-normalized mixed-case DOI, so the
  lower-cased gold key could never find them. Fixed in `ingest-local-pdf.py`
  (it now uses `_lib.normalize_doi` rather than a hand-rolled prefix strip), and
  5 pre-existing unreachable index keys were normalized or removed.
- `verified == 0` returned exit 0 as a clean SKIP even when every paper had
  ERRORed or drifted -- a green run reported because everything failed. It now
  skips only when nothing was ever attempted.

Also: LESSONS L-013, a CLAUDE.md hard rule, and the qa/review/iterate skills
updated to read the COVERAGE line rather than the PASS count, and to treat
PDF_DRIFT as "nothing was compared" rather than as a render defect.

highlights.message: fix(tests): 984 KB of published article text left the repo; sha256 pins replace it
highlights.body:
`tests/snapshots/*.txt` were 12 byte-identical `extract_pdf()` outputs of real
published papers -- title, authors, affiliations, full body -- git-tracked and
live on a PUBLIC remote since 2026-05-07. `apa_efendic_affect.txt` carried
SAGE's own reuse notice verbatim. Plaintext is *more* scrapable than the PDFs
this repo already refuses to commit.

A sha256 asserts exactly the same byte-for-byte guarantee in ~1 KB and asserts
nothing about anyone's copyright. `tests/snapshots/checksums.json` now pins the
digest, byte count and `method` per fixture; the pins were generated from the
old `.txt` files and then re-derived from a live extraction run, which matched
digest-for-digest before anything was deleted.

What a hash cannot do is print a diff, so that capability is restored rather
than dropped:

  --snapshot-explain  dumps the actual text to tmp/ (gitignored) AND diffs it
                      against the custodian's copy, fetched from article-finder
                      by the paper's DOI
  --snapshot-update   re-pins after an intentional extraction change

The 12 texts now live in article-finder as versioned tool artifacts
(`extract-text__docpluck@2.4.126`), keyed by DOI, outside every repo. Verified
end-to-end: with a pin deliberately corrupted, --snapshot-explain fetched the
custodian copy and produced a 0-byte diff (contents identical).

Also added, because the absence of each is what let this sit for three months:

- `test_no_article_text_in_snapshot_dir` -- watched FAIL against the 12 real
  files before they were removed. A shape check on the directory, not a
  filename denylist: these files were named exactly like ordinary fixtures,
  which is why three filename-based cleanup passes walked past them.
- `test_checksums_cover_every_manifest_fixture` -- coverage is asserted, not
  counted at runtime. The same defect class as the 24-skipped run this suite
  shipped for four days.
- `canonical_key` (the DOI) on every MANIFEST fixture.

Swept the full 478-commit history with a new content-based detector
(`article-finder/publication-text-scan.py`): these 12 files, in 28 blob
revisions, are the ONLY publication text this repo has ever held. No PDF was
ever committed; `tests/golden/`, the manifest and `scripts/harness/` are clean.

Full suite: 2088 passed, 166 skipped, 3 xfailed.

highlights.body:
Second, max-effort pass over the v2.4.126 work. The first pass fixed the
reported bug; sweeping for the CLASS found three more library defects, and
three review rounds found more defects in the fix than the fix had found in

Receipt (get_version_info): 3 keys -> 18. Beyond the first pass it now also

and unicodedata_version, since normalize.py calls unicodedata.normalize.
Engine versions come from installed distribution metadata, NOT the imported
module's __version__: preferring the module made opencv_version read
4.13.0.92 before `import cv2` and 4.13.0 after, one process, one install,
two answers. Stated cost: a shadowing module is not detected.

render_pdf_to_markdown(normalization_level=) was a SILENT NO-OP -- accepted,
documented as forwarded, discarded; none/standard/academic gave byte-identical
markdown. extract_sections now takes the level and applies it. The default
moved standard->academic (what the code actually did) so output is unchanged
for callers who never passed it.

Section.subheadings (v1.6.1) reached NO consumer -- the CLI and the service
had each independently enumerated the nine pre-v1.6.1 keys. Section.to_dict
/ SectionedDocument.to_dict now derive from fields().

append_footnotes_section was dead twice over (zero call sites; unreachable
precondition) while docpluck-review SKILL.md described it as live. Removed.

Not fixed, documented and queued: Section.pages is always () on every format
(page mapping needs layout=, which the sections path deliberately omits per
L-001; wiring it is a corpus-wide change needing its own gated cycle).

Perf: count_greek_chars was 60x slower than a regex (247s vs 4s across the
requester's 8,431-doc corpus); a correctness fix then called
packages_distributions() per engine (6-11s a call, uncached by the stdlib),
taking get_version_info() from ms to 24s. Now 122ms first call, 13ms after.

highlights.message: fix(normalize): strip BIDI FORMAT marks in S6 (v2.4.125)
highlights.body:
An invisible U+200E LEFT-TO-RIGHT MARK survived normalization into
rendered output immediately after a citation's closing paren
(xiao_2021_crsp: `Connolly, Reb, and Kausel (2013)<U+200E>`).

The S6 invisible-character block already stripped U+200B/C/D and
U+FEFF but SKIPPED U+200E/U+200F -- an omission in a sequence, not a
design decision. Now also strips U+2060 WORD JOINER, same class.

This is a CORRECTNESS defect, not cosmetics. An invisible character
inside rendered output breaks STRING EQUALITY and SEARCH for every
downstream consumer: a citation checker comparing `(2013)` against
`(2013)<LRM>` sees a mismatch it cannot see on screen -- and docpluck's
output feeds exactly such consumers (citelink, a downstream consumer). Same
rationale already recorded for the adjacent U+00AD strip ("invisible,
breaks search").

NORMALIZATION_VERSION -> 1.9.50.

Verification:
- 9 new tests, each watched FAILING at unfixed HEAD first (7 failed /
  2 passed -- the 2 passing prove the pre-existing U+200B/C/D/FEFF
  strips still work, so the red was specific to the new class).
- Strip effectiveness verified on a synthetic positive BEFORE the
  guard-diff, so a zero result is trustworthy rather than a false green.
- Corpus guard-diff, all 101 PDFs: 100 byte-identical BY CONSTRUCTION
  (they contain no bidi mark at all); the 1 touched is xiao, with
  exactly the 2 reported marks. Zero false positives possible.
- Idempotency + normalize guards: 41 passed, 0 failed.
- Full suite: 2015 passed, 190 skipped, 3 xfailed, 0 failed.
  Reconciles exactly as 2006 pre-existing + 9 new; skips and xfails
  unchanged, so zero behavioural drift.

Found via the run-7 triage of the open canary findings.

highlights.message: docs: TRIPLE AI VERIFICATION hard rule + re-audit of every prior won't-fix
highlights.body:
User directive 2026-08-05, portfolio-wide: "triple ai verifications always,
first you, then codex, then sonnet... these are science platforms, we need 100%
accuracy, no mistakes, no hallucinations."

WHAT WENT WRONG. I rejected a verifier's finding (docpluck drops the eta-squared-p
symbol) by asking pdftotext and pdfplumber whether the glyph was there -- the two
extractors whose flaws this library exists to correct. Getting 0 from both, I filed
"never encoded, OCR-tier, won't-fix" and wrote a shared lesson card teaching that
method. Rasterizing the page (pdftoppm -r 300) showed it plainly prints
"(eta^2_p = .000, 95% CI [.000, .003])". I then OVER-corrected: a pdfminer dump made
the whole clause look missing and I briefly reported published statistics were lost
-- also wrong, a pdfminer two-column reflow artifact.

Done properly (rasterize -> codex -> sonnet), all three passes converge: the symbol
is 4 filled bezier curves (fill=True, non_stroking_color=0.0, NO fontname -- font
glyph outlines would be object_type 'char') arranged as eta + superscript-2 +
subscript-p against the text baseline, with no char object in the gap. A second
identical cluster 13pt below proves it systematic. Genuinely OCR/shape-recognition
tier -- though codex noted a deterministic vector-path recogniser is a real non-OCR
route, so it is NOT closed forever.

RE-AUDIT OF ALL PRIOR REJECTIONS (an internal working doc).
Every past won't-fix used the same circular method, so all were re-opened.
TWO OF FOUR WERE WRONG:

- ar_apa ".245 painted minus" -> WRONG TWICE OVER. The page reads "beta = .245",
  POSITIVE, no minus anywhere, and there are 0 curves at the site. The ruling
  defended a character that does not exist, and its "OCR-tier" label masked the REAL
  defect (Greek beta in font AdvPSMP10 read as ASCII 'b' -- the W0m class, fixed in
  v2.4.117; current output is correct). This ruling was cited as THE PRECEDENT for
  the eta-squared won't-fix: a bad reject does not lose one defect, it propagates.
- efendic T2 "OCR-tier" -> WRONG (a detect.py whitespace-dilution bug, fixed v2.4.101).
- maier eta-squared-p -> upheld, but ONLY the curve geometry ever supported it.
- chan_feldman "alpha = 0.94 gold defect" -> upheld on SOURCE evidence: page 9 carries
  BOTH values on DIFFERENT scales (0.94 avoidance, 0.89 revenge); the gold attached
  the revenge value to the avoidance sentence.

Run 4's handoff called its evidence "airtight". It was not. Both that handoff and
this run's are corrected in place rather than left standing.

ENCODED PORTFOLIO-WIDE (not just this project):
- ~/Vibe/CLAUDE.md -- top-level hard rule; explicitly covers REJECTING a finding;
  standing obligation to re-open rejections whenever the standard rises.
- docpluck/CLAUDE.md -- same rule in the project hard-rules list.
- _shared/lessons/triple-ai-verification-mandatory-for-science-claims.md
- _shared/lessons/never-adjudicate-an-extraction-defect-with-the-extractors.md
- memory feedback_triple_ai_verification_always + MEMORY.md index
- DELETED the bad card written earlier this session that taught the circular method.
- ~/Vibe/todo.md -- 7 suspect won't-fix rulings queued across a downstream consumer,
  a downstream consumer and 2Rmarkdown, cross-project REPLY docs first (a wrong reject that
  crosses a repo boundary closes the item on both sides).

highlights.message: fix(normalize,sections): wrapped-CONTACT strip + KEYWORDS label/value split (v2.4.124)
highlights.body:
Publisher furniture was splitting a sentence in half, and a keyword list was
being read as the Introduction's first sentence.

NORMALIZATION_VERSION -> 1.9.49; SECTIONING_VERSION -> 1.2.4.

1. Wrapped-CONTACT block (normalize.py, P0)

xiao_2021_crsp rendered the T&F correspondence footer INSIDE a body sentence:
"The target and the / CONTACT Gilad Feldman / Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR /
competitor form a core choice set". The v2.4.6 rule requires CONTACT + name +
email on ONE line; T&F column-wraps the block so each lands on its own line.

Four of the block's six lines were ALREADY stripped by sibling patterns, so
this was a PARTIAL strip -- worse than none, because it removes exactly the
lines that made the block recognisable as furniture and welds the residue into
prose. When auditing a strip rule, check what its NEIGHBOURS already remove.

Keyed on the structural signature (line-initial all-caps CONTACT followed only
by a personal name), never paper identity. A _CONTACT_NON_NAME_WORDS veto keeps
nav furniture ("CONTACT Details Below"). The orphaned "<City>, <Region>" tail is
removed ONLY by adjacency to a dropped opener -- never on its own shape, since a
bare "Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR" is ordinary prose (a test pins that it survives
alone). The wrapped pattern deliberately does NOT live in
_PAGE_FOOTER_LINE_PATTERNS: the generic any()-match would drop vetoed lines
before the veto branch could run.

2. KEYWORDS label/value split (sections/core.py)

highlights.message: fix(normalize): refuse a sign flip against a CI that cannot hold a negative (v2.4.123)
highlights.body:
docpluck rendered an IMPOSSIBLE F-statistic. maier Table 9's row is

    Target article | 1, 114 | 2.00 | .16 | N/A | .02 | [.00, .09]

-- an F, its p, its partial eta-squared, and the CI OF THE ETA-SQUARED. W0d
(recover_minus_via_ci_pairing) repairs a font corruption where a minus is read
as '2', accepting the flip when the corrected value lands inside a paired CI and
the literal does not. It paired the F-statistic with the eta-squared's CI: -.00
is inside [.00, .09] and 2.00 is not, so it fired, and the render carried

    F = -.00

An F-statistic is a ratio of sums of squares -- non-negative by construction --
so the output was not merely wrong but arithmetically impossible. Both text
channels confirm the source reads 2.00; the library manufactured the sign.

Fix: refuse the pairing when the CI's LOWER bound is >= 0. A wholly non-negative
interval cannot contain a negative, so containment is satisfiable only
degenerately (-.00 clipping the zero edge), which is evidence of MIS-PAIRING
rather than corruption. Keying on the interval's arithmetic instead of on F
specifically covers every non-negative statistic that can sit beside a
non-negative CI (F, chi-square, R2, eta2, odds ratios, variance components)
without enumerating them, and cannot disarm a genuine recovery -- a truly
negative estimate always has a CI admitting negatives.

Evidence:
- tests written against the unfixed code and watched FAIL, then pass;
- all 31 pre-existing W0d tests stay green, incl. the efendic B-column
  recoveries the rule exists for;
- corpus guard-diff, all 152 PDFs rendered twice (guard on vs off):
  2 false positives removed (the maier article and its a downstream consumer duplicate),
  0 regressions, every other paper byte-identical;
- suite 1962 passed, 3 xfail (the P1 table defects stay armed).

Companion to the REJECTED W0b-col recovery: that failed because column consensus
is not per-record evidence. This is the converse -- per-record containment IS the
right evidence, but only when the record paired is the right one. A containment
test silently assumes the CI belongs to the token it pairs with; verify that is
arithmetically possible first.

highlights.message: fix(normalize): a range bound is a number, not an interaction operator (v2.4.122)
highlights.body:
W0i's x-as-3 glyph recovery was rewriting RANGE BOUNDS as an operator inside
Camelot table cells. chan_feldman's Table-2 note rendered

    "Avoidance behaviour scores ranged from x to 15"

for a source that reads "from 3 to 15" -- the library DELETED a published scale
bound and wrote an operator in its place. Both text channels confirm the source
says 3; the raw-text channel rendered the same sentence correctly a hundred
lines earlier, so one document carried the same fact right and wrong at once.

Not paper-specific: any "from 3 to N" / "between 3 and N" reaching a table cell
was affected, in any publisher's paper.

Root cause: W0i's only pre-digit guard was _TIMES_REFERENCE_WORD_RE, a list of
reference NOUNS (Model|Study|Table|Figure|...) that makes "Model 3 predictor" a
genuine ordinal. "from" is not a reference noun, so the guard had nothing to
say, while "from 3 to" matches W0i's letter-space-3-space-letter signature
exactly. A vocabulary list cannot defend a grammatical position -- it is always
missing the next word.

Fix: guard on the grammatical FRAME instead. A range is from|between BEFORE the
digit AND to|and|through|until AFTER it, with BOTH halves required -- a lone
trailing "to" could be a wrapped predictor ("Attitude 3 to risk"), and a lone
leading "from" is likewise ambiguous. A frame generalises across publishers.

Evidence:
- new tests written against the unfixed code and watched FAIL, then pass;
- full-corpus pdftotext sweep (all 152 PDFs): 8 range-frame-with-3 sites across
  5 distinct articles, out of 380 range frames overall -- all 5 pinned as
  regression cases. The sweep is why the guard covers "between ... and": maier's
  Bayes factors and bmc_med_3's lesion diameters use it, and a from-only guard
  would have left them exposed;
- targeted production-path guard-diff (each paper rendered twice, guard on vs
  off, so every difference is attributable to this change): 1 false positive
  removed, 0 regressions, all 8 canaries byte-identical;
- suite: 1959 passed, 3 xfail (the two P1 pinned table defects stay armed).

highlights.body:

unchanged: the normalize fix is complexity-only, matching is byte-identical.

Two false-negative classes in the guard that decides whether a whitespace/char
grid is a real DATA table:

(a) _CAPTION_LABEL_RE was UNANCHORED, so a mid-sentence CROSS-REFERENCE in a
    footnote/prose cell ("...al. (2007) in Table 8.", "...in Figure 2. We
    summarized...") read as an absorbed caption and condemned the whole grid.
    An absorbed caption always BEGINS its cell; a reference has sentence text
    before it. Anchored to ^\s*, matching the discipline
    camelot_extract._CAPTION_ROW_PATTERN already documents (its comment notes
    anchoring is why an inline "see Table 2" does not match).

(b) the clean-data-cell test matched a SINGLE numeric token, so every
    multi-token APA COMPOSITE scored as non-data: 2.84 [1.89] (mean [SD]),
    3.47 [1.23] (170) (mean [SD] (n)), 2.84 +/- 1.89, 0.42***. A descriptives
    table built from them scored clean_data_rows=0 and was discarded as prose.
    Replaced the shape regex with a NUMERIC-DOMINANCE test (_cell_is_clean_data:
    digit-bearing AND free of substantive words), which generalises instead of
    chasing each composite with another alternation. The prose side is unmoved,
    so absorbed body text is still rejected.

101-PDF guard-diff: 24 tables recover (up from 20 at v2.4.120), 0 regressed,
0 foreign-caption acceptances.

A SECOND quadratic regex, and why the first fix looked complete but wasn't:
v2.4.120 bounded _CI_UPPER_DROPPED_RE and reported the ReDoS resolved. It was
not — normalize_text still scaled ~4-5x per doubling. It was missed because the
check was an absolute WALL-CLOCK budget, which passed alone and failed only
under parallel load, so it read as flakiness. Rewritten as a SCALING RATIO
(load-independent: contention inflates both measurements together) it failed
consistently, turning noise into signal.

Instrumenting every COMPILED pattern's .sub() via re.compile interception (a
module-level sweep misses these — they live inside a list literal, and reported
0.000s) attributed 3.165s of 3.7s at n=20000 to the Royal Society running-footer
pattern in _WATERMARK_PATTERNS, whose leading unbounded \d+ starts a match
attempt at every digit and then fails. Bounding it to \d{1,6} (a page number is
never longer) is ~1370x faster on the pattern (4.53s -> 0.0033s) and ~50x
end-to-end (normalize_text 4.85s -> 0.044s at n=20000), now genuinely linear at
~2.0x per doubling, with both real footer forms matched identically. A
lookahead-anchored variant was tried first and MEASURED WORSE (6.4s vs 3.2s) —
discarded rather than reasoned about.

This permanently removes the flakiness from
test_regex_no_catastrophic_backtracking, which prior handoffs recorded as a
load-sensitive perf test. It was a real, long-standing performance defect all
along. Full suite also runs ~10 min faster (24:51 vs 37:19).

highlights.message: test(tables): pin the _cluster_into_rows chain-merge defect (attempted fix REVERTED)

_cluster_into_rows measures the y-gap to the PREVIOUS WORD, not the row's anchor.
Words sort by (top, x0), so in a table with wrapped or vertically staggered cells
the running 'previous top' creeps forward in sub-threshold steps and the threshold
is never crossed — an unbounded chain merge. chan_feldman Table 3 holds 266 words
at 47 distinct y-positions with 0.3-7.4pt gaps against an 11.4pt threshold, and
clusters into 3 rows spanning 240pt: a 10-row table smeared into 3, which then

excellent (chan T3 3->22 rows; T2 0->108 cells; T9 0->14 cells; maier T8/T11
gained cells) but it broke 9 real-PDF tests across 4 files, because a real row
can legitimately be TALL: xiao Table 4's row 2 spans 94.4pt as a multi-line
stacked data block, and a hard anchor cap shatters it. The previous-word test
under-splits; a naive anchor cap over-splits. Neither rule alone is correct.

fix XPASSes loudly, plus three plain-assert companions pinning behaviour that must
not regress while it is solved. FINDINGS doc records the measurements and three

signature detection; derive the row grid from the most stable column).

highlights.message: fix(tables): a table's own caption no longer condemns its own table (v2.4.120)
highlights.body:
RC-T cycle 4. _whitespace_grid_is_clean rejects any grid containing a
"Table N."/"Figure N." cell — the signature of a region that absorbed a
NEIGHBOURING table's caption. But _region_for_caption builds every region as
_union(caption_bbox, geom_bbox), so a caption-anchored region ALWAYS contains
its own caption by construction. The guard therefore condemned EVERY region
grid: whitespace_cells returned 0 cells corpus-wide (19/19 chan_feldman+maier
regions) and each table fell to the raw_text fallback, which truncates rows.
The guard's own comment said the marker proves the region absorbed "an adjacent
table's (or its own) caption" — the "or its own" clause was the bug.

The exemption is IDENTITY-based, not position-based: the anchoring caption's
number is threaded from the region spec / region.caption_match into the guard,
and a caption cell is exempt only when it names THAT exact number, sits in a
leading row, and is the first such match — per-CELL, and opt-in so the
auto-detect path keeps the strict legacy behaviour.

A position-only draft was written and REJECTED in cross-model review (codex);
all three of its holes reproduced locally: a neighbour's caption in a leading
row blessed as "own" (publishing another table's data), (r,c) sort order picking
the leftmost caption on side-by-side pages, and a whole-ROW exemption letting a
second Table/Figure caption ride along. Each is pinned by a regression test.
